Coding/CSS-ideas.title: CSS ideas
Coding/CSS-ideas.richContent:
Colors

First define your basic colors using OKLCH.

Then, you can use native CSS functions like color-mix() to modify these base colors:

This feels much more intuitive, and more controlled, than coming up with various hex values and sprinkling them throughout your stylesheets.

Spacing

Use character width for horizontal spacing, and rem for vertical spacing

References

  • Vanilla CSS is all you need
  • Modern CSS patterns in Campfire

Coding/Quartz-customizations/Disable-Fol.filePath: Coding/Quartz customizations/Disable Folder Listings for certain index pages.md
Coding/Quartz-customizations/Disable-Fol.title: Disable Folder Listings for certain index pages
Coding/Quartz-customizations/Disable-Fol.richContent:
Quartz automatically generates index pages for folders, and shows a list of all pages under that folder.

You can create your own index.md file to change the title and add any content you want, but disabling the list of pages was not as easy.

I ended up editing FolderContent.txs directly, to look for an option called hideFolderContent in the page frontmatter.

This wraps the portion of the page that shows folder content in a conditional, which can be toggled off by adding a variable to any page’s frontmatter.

Coding/Quartz-customizations/Links.title: Links
Coding/Quartz-customizations/Links.content:
I’m basically creating a new type of post called a Link, which consists of a link to an external site + my brief comments about it. Making this work the way I want will take a bit of tweaking.
Pagination
Pagination doesn’t exist on Quartz! This is a pretty big difference from the traditional blog structure, so I need to consider how I want to format my content.
Probably the easiest option is to divide my content into pages by year (or quarterly or monthly if I end up with too many pages) as an archival view, and have a list of the most recent ones somewhere on the home page.
I already organize the files into folders by year, so that should not be hard.
Customize the list display.
By default, Quartz shows the date, the title as a link to the page, and tags.

 Hide the tags. They take up too much space.
 Make the title link to the source URL

Get this from the file frontmatter


 Show the page content directly under the link

It’s short enough that there shouldn’t be a need to click through.



Hide files in the Explorer
There are going to be a lot of files, and a lot of them probably will have long names.
For just the Links folder (and probably Posts too) I don’t want the explorer to list every page. Honestly, probably just having the parent folder shown open will be good enough.

Coding/direnv.title: direnv
Coding/direnv.content:
direnv lets you define environment variables to be loaded only within certain directories. It’s a great way to save secret variables that are project-specific, without cluttering your global shell config.
Installation
brew install direnv
echo 'eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"' >> ~/.zshrc

Usage
echo 'export SECRET_TOKEN="super-secret"' > .envrc
echo 'export API_KEY="12345"' >> .envrc
direnv allow

Whenever you cd into this folder, the environment variables will load.
Don’t commit the secrets!
Add to .gitignore:
.envrc

Colophon.title: Colophon
Colophon.content:
This site is build with Quartz v4, which is a static-site generator that transforms a folder of Markdown files into a website.
It’s designed to work well with Obsidian’s features, and that is what I use to write my content. I’m not that deep in the Obsidian ecosystem, and I don’t really use any advanced features, but everything about it, especially PC/Mobile cross-functionality, is pretty good.
Because I access my Obsidian Vault on both desktop and mobile, the vault is saved in a weird location in my iCloud drive:
~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/Obsidian/

When building this site with Quartz, I have a script that batch-copies the files from my Obsidian vault into the Quartz folder, which it then uses to generate the site. The generated site is pushed to Github, where I have an Action setup to copy the contents of the public/ folder to my VPS.
I’ve always felt that it’s unwieldy to install static-site generators on the VPS, so I prefer to do the generation on my local machine and just copy over the outputted files.
Since the Markdown content is synced via iCloud, I can even set up a cron task on my home computer to build + deploy every hour.

Games/Chaos-Zero-Nightmare/Duplicating-c.title: Duplicating cards effectively
Games/Chaos-Zero-Nightmare/Duplicating-c.content:
A lot of characters benefit greatly from having a key card duplicated as many times as possible. One time is good, but two times (or even more?) is fantastic.
Remove other Epiphany cards
Each Copy Card event in Chaos randomly selects 3 cards, of which you choose 1 to copy. If you want your target card to appear as one of the choices, one strategy is to remove as many alternatives as possible.
Instead of removing basic cards right away, you can instead remove other characters’ unique cards. By sacrificing their deck’s strength, you can build one deck to be especially strong.
This is easier to pull off after your characters have developed a fair amount, as survival becomes less of an issue.
Unique cards
Some characters have cards with the Unique attribute, which means they can’t be copied. Some cards gain Unique from Epiphanies. Since Unique cards will not be chosen as Copy targets, you don’t need to remove them in preparation for Copy events.
Pairing characters with these cards will make it a little bit easier to copy the card you are targeting.
The first boss is key
It’s much easier to duplicate your target cards at the first boss fight. By the time you reach the second, you just have too many cards to control it effectively.
If you haven’t duplicated your target card at the first boss fight, that might be a good time to reset your run.

Games/Chaos-Zero-Nightmare/Farming-Strat.title: Farming Strategy
Games/Chaos-Zero-Nightmare/Farming-Strat.content:
Laboratory 0 
                  
                

A lot of this information may be specific to farming on Laboratory 0. I’ll need to update this if mechanics change in the next event.


Here are a list of some general tips to farming Chaos to build strong decks for your characters.
Chaos Difficulty
The best difficulty to farm is considered to be Difficulty 8, for a few reasons:

Enemy levels increase a lot when moving up to 9
8 with Nightmare mode gives consistent access to Tier 13-14 save data, which is generally enough to fit the decks you want.

Chaos Effects
Some effects are much easier to manage than others. Things like:

Decrease health (take damage) at beginning of each turn
Increase Elite and Boss HP & Damage
Increase number of Elite fights
Decrease max health

are not too bad. Especially for Laboratory 0, the scary monsters who can end your run are actually in normal fights. So choosing Elite fights has a lot of benefits.
The bad effects you want to avoid are:

Enemies gain Morale/Fortify after X turns
Enemies gain Morale/Fortify upon enemy death

because these can create impossible fights that will wipe your run.
Reducing credits is fine if you just want to finish the runs, but if you’re trying to build a great deck you need a fair amount of credits to remove cards, buy neutral cards, and buy equipment. So events within Chaos that give credits are pretty valuable.
Chaos Upgrades
There is an upgrade in the Chaos system that increases the chance of encountering Rare Species (upgraded versions of normal enemies) by up to 45%. The problem with this is that sometimes the enemies are strong enough to end your run, while the only upside is that you get more Chaos Orbs.
However! If you reset your Chaos Upgrades, all tiers remain unlocked and you can choose which upgrades to enable. And you get all of our Chaos Orbs back.
So just reset, and re-enable everything except for the Rare Species probably up. Profit.

I have a few good +1AP epiphanies on my Draw cards, so I ended up having a lot of AP left over. I may even be able to drop Mika for Veronica if I ever draw her.
My second team remains an unsolved issue, though. I’m going to stick with Renoa + Nia, so if my third is not Cassius then maybe Rei? Or maybe even move Mika over here.

Site-todo.title: Site todo
Site-todo.content:
In addition to using this site as a general wiki for my thoughts, I’m eyeing the possibility of migrating my entire blog to this format. I Currently make my site with Jekyll (a great product!) but I have a lot of customization living in each post’s frontmatter, and while I do have a variety of convenience scripts set up, I kind of need to be sitting at my desktop machine in order to create and publish posts.
With Quartz, I just add a new file somewhere, slap on a few words, and it’s already a part of my website. I want to see if there is a way to stay within this dead-simple workflow, and somehow recreate the functionality of my current site.
Todos

Game wiki section

 Start writing things about games I am playing
 Micro-posts

 Start writing micro-posts for my thoughts while playing
 Set up a workflow to easily write/save new files with the correct name and location (Obsidian script, or Shortcuts?)
 Display a game’s micro posts on that game’s top page




Other

 Set up automatic deploys (rsync) in Github Actions
 Disable Folder Listings for certain index pages
 Make a section for Haiku?
 Decide how much I want to change the site’s layout/CSS
 Enable hover hover-over links for only certain links

Just definitions would be ideal

index.title: Invisible Wiki
index.content:
This is a freeform space for me to build – and hopefully grow – a personal knowledge-base. My main website is a space for my thoughts and longer written posts, and has more information about me.
Some main categories of this wiki are:

The Games section where I write about the games I play. This includes information that I collect for me reference while playing, as well as a record of thoughts that I have about the game experience.
The Coding section where I collect snippets of information about programming. I’ll also use it as a working document while I configure and update this site.

And I guess that’s all for now.
